correctness.rationale: For the target distance R sampled once and held fixed, the conditional Laplace transform is F_R(s)=(r+s)e^{-R sqrt((r+s)/D)}/[s+r e^{-R sqrt((r+s)/D)}]. Differentiation yields E[T|R]=(e^{qR}-1)/r and E[T^2|R]=(2e^{2qR}-(2+qR)e^{qR})/r^2. Integrating against lambda exp(-lambda R) proves the stated first/second moments, finite iff q<lambda and 2q<lambda respectively. Rescaling Y_R=r e^{-qR}T makes its transforms converge uniformly on a small complex neighborhood to 1/(1+w), hence fixed integer moments tend to m!, giving the exact all-moment criterion mq<lambda. Algebraic optimization of 1/[D lambda^2 z(1-z)] yields mean optimum z=1/2; of 1/[z(1-2z)]-1 yields CV optimum z=1/4, CV²=7 and mean cost factor 4/3. Independent symbolic differentiation/integrals verified the finite formulas; divergence and uniqueness follow analytically.

value.rationale: The broad fixed-random-target setting has known mean-optimal Poisson resetting, but a natural reliability question is whether variance remains finite and which rate optimizes dispersion. The sharp integer-moment thresholds, infinite variance at the known mean optimum, and distinct exact CV-optimum with small mean cost are concrete mathematically useful boundary phenomena.

limitations: One-dimensional Brownian diffusion, strictly positive homogeneous reset rate, and one fixed exponential target; integer m>=1 only, not fractional moments or resampled-target protocols.
